consensus_summary: Grapes are multivalent but center on the fruit of God's vineyard/people: good grapes as spiritual fruitfulness, faithfulness, blessing/abundance, or (via wine) Christ's blood; wild/sour grapes as unfaithfulness/sin; pressed grapes as divine wrath/judgment.
book_summary: Grapes are a people's works ripened into persons as the vineyard's yield; when pressed they yield covenant wine or the blood of judgment according to whether the vintage is good or wild.
consensus_core_identification: fruit (good or wild) expected from God's people/vineyard, with secondary strands of blessing, Eucharistic wine, and wrath when pressed
book_core_identification: a people's works matured into persons (vineyard yield) whose pressing yields covenant wine or judgment-blood by vintage quality
boundary_disagreement: Consensus treats grapes chiefly as abstract fruit/works/righteousness (or wine/blood); book restricts the yield to persons produced by works and makes the good/wild pressing outcome the explicit dual product.
rationale: Both share the Isa 5 vineyard frame, good-vs-wild distinction, and pressed-grape outcomes (covenant blessing vs wrath). The book keeps that referent category but materially tightens it by equating the ripened yield specifically with persons (supported by Mic 7's link of missing clusters to missing upright men) rather than leaving fruit as moral qualities or generic abundance; Eucharistic and pure-land-blessing readings are backgrounded rather than denied. This is boundary refinement, not core replacement.
strongest_objection: Consensus primaries frequently foreground Eucharistic blood or land-abundance as co-equal with fruitfulness; the book's 'works-into-persons' gloss and exclusive dual-pressing formula could be seen as over-specifying beyond the plain sense of the listed texts.
